 Rugby League World Cup finals live: Kangaroos face New Zealand after Jillaroos win fourth title
 J By Jon Healy
 Topic: Rugby League
 Posted Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 2:57pm Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 2:57pm Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 2:57pm , updated Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 7:23pm Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 7:23pm Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 7:23pm Skip to timeline abc.net.au/news/kangaroos-jillaroos-live-rugby-league-world-cup-finals/107376474 Link copied Share Share article The Kangaroos take on New Zealand in the men's Rugby League World Cup final after the Jillaroos won their fourth straight title with a 34-10 win over the Kiwi Ferns in the women's decider.
 Follow all the action in our live blog below and tune in to our live radio coverage .

 Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 7:29pm Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 7:29pm Here come the teams
 J By Jon Healy
 Isaah Yeo is leading out the Kangaroos, alongside former premiership teammate James Fisher-Harris out front for the Kiwis.
 But the New Zealanders are making the Aussies wait.
 The anthems and then the haka are ahead of us.
 React React Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 7:27pm Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 7:27pm The energy is building at Lang Park
 J By Jon Healy
 The teams are delivering their last messages in the sheds.
 The crowd's building.
 The light show is going off.
 We're not far away now from the 2026 Men's Rugby League World Cup final.
 React React Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 7:17pm Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 7:17pm Walsh's moment
 J By Jon Healy
 (Getty) Reece Walsh's Broncos endured a historically bad premiership defence and he barely played State of Origin for the defeated Queensland Maroons this year.
 But a maiden World Cup win could make that all a distant memory.
 Does he have one last masterclass in him?
 React React Key Event
 Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 7:12pm Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 7:12pm LATE MAIL: Latrell Mitchell confirmed out for Kangaroos
 J By Jon Healy
 (NRL.com) So, Latrell Mitchell has succumbed to his illness and can't join the bench, replaced by James Tedesco, losing a little more versatility from a team already lacking in it.
 For the Kiwis, Ronaldo Mulitalo returns from suspension to take his place on the wing.
 React React Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 6:56pm Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 6:56pm Men's World Cup winners history
 J By Jon Healy
 Let's have a look back at some Rugby League World Cup history.
 The Kangaroos have won 12 men's Rugby League World Cups, including nine of the past 10, which doesn't leave much room for anyone else to have broken through over the years.
 Despite being the de facto number two in the world for the past few decades, New Zealand has only one crown, in 2008; while Great Britain won three, including the inaugural 1954 final against France, and the 1960 and 1972 deciders.
 So that's:
 Australia – 12: 1957, 1968, 1970, 1975, 1977, 1988, 1992, 1995, 2000, 2013, 2017, 2022
 Great Britain – 3: 1954, 1960, 1972
 New Zealand – 1: 2008
 React React Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 6:36pm Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 6:36pm A culmination for Kelly
 J By Jon Healy
 Coach Jess Skinner and captain Isabelle Kelly are beaming behind the podium.
 Kelly is asked about how this team, which seems almost unbeatable, stays motivated.
 "When you wear the Jillaroos jersey you're always striving to be the best," Kelly says.
 It's a culmination of a long journey for the Australian skipper.
 "I'm nearly 10 years into this jersey I came in as quite a young girl."
 Kelly says players like Ruan Sims, Ali Brigginshaw and Renee Kunst "really shaped me to be the player I am today".
 "I feel very honoured that we were able to get the job done."
 And she counts the retiring Millie Elliott as one of those women.
 React React Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 6:31pm Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 6:31pm It turns out winners actually are grinners
 J By Jon Healy
 (Getty) (Getty) (Getty) (Getty) React React Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 6:21pm Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 6:21pm Jess Skinner gets the Gatorade shower
 J By Jon Healy
 Jaime Chapman and Jess Sergis sneak away from celebrations to grab the cooler and sneak up on Jess Skinner, who wins the World Cup in her first time as coach.
 Meanwhile, the players are still celebrating in the streamers while ground staff are raking them up.
 React React Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 6:18pm Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 6:18pm Isabelle Kelly thanks the Ferns for a proper fight
 J By Jon Healy
 It may have looked easy in the first half, but Jillaroos captain Isabelle Kelly thanks them for a great game.
 "It's been such a great rivalry for so many years now. We were really excited to come up against the best of the best and thank you for such a great game."
 Kelly reserves special praise for the squad players who didn't get on the field today, including Ellie Johnston, Julia Robinson, Jocelyn Kelleher, Makenzie Weale, Sarah Togatuki and Quincy Dodd.
 They're all welcomed into the team photo for the trophy lift as Tina Turner's Simply The Best rings out.
 React React Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 6:13pm Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 6:13pm Georgia Hale promises the Kiwi Ferns are coming
 J By Jon Healy
 The New Zealand captain is clearly disappointed but incredibly proud of her team and her country, especially the fans who followed them all around the tournament, form Newcastle, to Christchurch, to the Gold Coast, back to Newy, and up here to Brisbane.
 "As a proud Kiwi girl, thank you so much to all of our fierce and staunch supporters that have been with us throughout the tournament."
 New Zealand won the first three Women's World Cups, but has since lost the title of the world's best to Australia.
 Hale promises they'll be back.
 "The best of the Kiwi Ferns is still to be shown, so stay with us."
 React React Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 6:10pm Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 6:10pm Jaime Chapman is player of the match
 J By Jon Healy
 (ABC Sport: Zane Bojack) Tough to argue with that first-half hat-trick in a game without any second-half points.
 She also equalled the record for most tries in a World Cup, with 13.
 React React Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 6:08pm Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 6:08pm Emotional celebrations for Millie Elliott
 J By Jon Healy
 (Getty) The Jillaroos prop announced her retirement from rugby league and she goes out with another State of Origin, premiership and a World Cup victory (all of them unbeaten).
 One player who shared in all three of those with her, Keeley Nizza, can't hold back the tears as she talks about her great mate.
 "Millie's a champion, she's my best friend in the world, she's just the ultimate champion," she tells ABC Sport.
 "Sorry, I'm so emotional.
 Millie Elliott has been wrapped in hugs by all her teammates. (Getty) "There's no better competitor in the game, it's not a coincidence she's come back this year and we've gone undefeated.
 "I don't think there'll ever be a player like her. I'm incredibly lucky to get to play alongside her."
 React React Key Event
 Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 5:59pm Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 5:59pm FULL-TIME: The Jillaroos are four-time world champions!
 J By Jon Healy
 (Getty) Chantay Kiria-Ratu's conversion falls short to bring an end to proceedings, sparking celebrations out there for the Jillaroos, who beat New Zealand's Kiwi Ferns 34-10 in the final to win their fourth straight Women's Rugby League World Cup.
 Look, that second half was nothing to write home about for either side, but the Aussies earned that right with that dominant six-try first half.
 React React Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 5:57pm Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 5:57pm The latest of consolation tries for New Zealand
 J By Jon Healy
 The Kiwi Ferns try a chip over the right side and Isabelle Kelly gets back to reel it in, but she's monstered by Alexis Tauaneai, losing the ball and allowing Mackenzie Wiki to swoop and dive in for a late try.
 Remarkably, New Zealand ends the tournament without having conceded a single second-half point.
 React React Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 5:54pm Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 5:54pm 67' Isabelle Kelly says NO
 J By Jon Healy
 The Kiwi Ferns try one more time down the right through Mackenzie Wiki, but skipper Isabelle Kelly gets across to lasso her into touch in a phenomenal one-on-one tackle.
 React React Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 5:53pm Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 5:53pm 66' Apii Nicholls is down with a hamstring
 J By Jon Healy
 The New Zealand fullback has been one of the Kiwi Ferns' best tonight and her night ends in misery, going down like she's been hit by a sniper, grabbing at her hamstring and limping off the far side of the field.
 React React Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 5:52pm Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 5:52pm 65' We just can't buy a try now
 J By Jon Healy
 Jesse Southwell breaks through the middle and manages to offload to Kezie Apps, or should I say towards   Kezie Apps, as she can't reel in the ball from high above her head.
 This second half is just a points desert.
 React React Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 5:50pm Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 5:50pm A sell-out tonight
 J By Jon Healy
 Might as well talk about peripherals Jon. Decent crowd turn up to watch the Jillaroos game ?
 - Phillip 
 Hi Phillip,
 The crowd has grown throughout the game, which unfortunately means they've turned up mostly for what has been a really poor showing in this second half.
 It's a sell-out tonight.
 React React Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 5:46pm Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 5:46pm 61' Still we wait for our first points of the half
 J By Jon Healy
 A forward pass is thrown to Sariah Paki to end another set in disappointment for Australia. And the wait goes on for our first points since a 40-point first half.
 React React Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 5:43pm Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 5:43pm 58' Nasty head clash
 J By Jon Healy
 Simaima Taufa and Raecene McGregor are both down after a really heavy head clash. Both players will end the game in an HIA-enforced 15-minute break you'd think.
 The New Zealand halfback goes off, but Taufa is staying on despite being opened up by the contact.
 React React Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 5:42pm Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 5:42pm 58' Things are petering out
 J By Jon Healy
 Abbi Church drops a bomb from Jesse Southwell on the last to hand the ball to New Zealand.
 And this game is limping to the finish line.
 React React Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 5:37pm Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 5:37pm 54' Another chance blown by New Zealand
 J By Jon Healy
 The field position hasn't been that far in Australia's favour in this half, but the attack from New Zealand has been pretty ordinary.
 And this time the set ends with a rushed left-foot kick by Apii Nicholls that trickles dead.
 React React Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 5:36pm Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 5:36pm 53' Jillaroos keep turning up in defence
 J By Jon Healy
 The Kiwi Ferns are on the front foot after a break by Apii Nicholls.
 But the Jillaroos just keep turning up across the park to cut them off.
 Isabelle Kelly and Jaime Chapman are the prime movers.
 React React Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 5:33pm Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 5:33pm 51' Jillaroos keeping the pressure on
 J By Jon Healy
 Jesse Southwell pins New Zealand deep with a brilliant kick over the head of Mackenzie Wiki.
 They give away a penalty to give the Kiwi Ferns another piggyback upfield, but Tiana Penitani-Gray rattles the ball loose as Stacey Waaka takes a charge.
 React React Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 5:29pm Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 5:29pm 47' Church gives New Zealand a shot
 J By Jon Healy
 Abbi Church marks a bomb, then fumbles in the tackle, handing the Kiwi Ferns a full set inside the 10 metres.
 React React Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 5:26pm Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 5:26pm 45' Jillaroos bomb one
 J By Jon Healy
 (Getty) Olivia Kernick gets through the line with some lovely sleight of hand and has the chance to set up Kezie Apps, but she holds up the pass too long and gets hit as she throws it, missing the mark.
 React React Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 5:25pm Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 5:25pm 44' Another successful captain's challenge
 J By Jon Healy
 Isabelle Kelly wins another captain's challenge as the Jillaroos are called for a knock-on before the Kiwi Ferns fumbled on a left-side shift.
 Replays back up the Jillaroos and they keep the ball.
 React React Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 5:23pm Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 5:23pm 42' Free metres for the Kiwi Ferns
 J By Jon Healy
 Jesse Southwell rolls in a grubber and Apii Nicholls gets back to clean it up. She turns back upfield and is whacked high by Isabelle Kelly.
 Then, first tackle after the touch finder, Tiana Penitani-Gray is pinged for a lifting tackle on Stacey Waaka.
 Piggy-backing the New Zealanders over halfway.
 React React Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 5:20pm Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 5:20pm 40' Try-saver from New Zealand
 J By Jon Healy
 The Jillaroos are surging on New Zealand's tryline and challenge all over the width of the field.
 Eventually Tarryn Aiken pokes her nose through as she cuts back against the grain, but she's stopped just a metre short.
 Loading Twitter content React React Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 5:18pm Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 5:18pm 37' No-one wants the footy
 J By Jon Healy
 The Kiwi Ferns try a chip over the top and Jess Sergis takes a great one-handed grab in the face of a couple of very offside chasers.
 She breaks through and looks to offload to Tamika Upton, who would have surely gone the rest of the way, but she's thrown it over her head to Mele Hufanga. Then she fumbles and it ends up with the Jillaroos again.
 Belinda Sharpe says Australia knocked on, but Isabelle Kelly challenges, and it's successful again. The Jillaroos get the ball back.
 React React Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 5:14pm Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 5:14pm 36' Jillaroos kick off the second half
 J By Jon Healy
 And find no man's land! But Chantay Kiria-Ratu manages to rein it in before the gold jerseys arrive.
 React React Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 5:07pm Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 5:07pm Longer half-time break
 J By Jon Healy
 The heat out there has prompted organisers to lengthen half-time by about five minutes.
 React React Key Event
 Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 4:55pm Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 4:55pm HALF-TIME: The Jillaroos dominating New Zealand 34-6
 J By Jon Healy
 (Getty) That was an utter demolition job from the Jillaroos in the opening 35 minutes.
 After getting shocked out of the gates by Fiji last week, there was no such ambush this time around, with the Aussies showing their skill and class from the jump this time and nabbing six tries.
 I'm not sure which is hotter: The Jillaroos' form or the weather in Brisbane.
 But hat-trick hero Jaime Chapman says Australia wants more.
 "It feels like Bali, I'm going there next week," she tells Channel Seven, acknowledging the job's not done.
 "We're fitter, we're stronger and we'll come out next half and give it to them again."
 React React Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 4:52pm Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 4:52pm Sunday's a great day for Church!
 J By Jon Healy
 The Jillaroos line up out to the right and it's just pure class all across the park as Tarryn Aiken, after hitting Shaylee Bent with a short ball on the previous play out this side, this time goes out the back and Tamika Upton burns Mele Hufanga for pass to unleash Abbi Church, who returns the ball to her fullback to dive in.
 React React Key Event
 Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 4:47pm Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 4:47pm It's a spectacular hat-trick for Jaime Chapman!
 J By Jon Healy
 It's a carbon copy of Jess Sergis's effort, but maybe even more impressive as Jaime Chapman storms onto the football just off the ruck and bursts through the first line of defence.
 She breaks through the tackle of Apii Nicholls, runs backwards for five metres, but still has enough pace and strength to skip away from Stacey Waaka and finish off another 70-metre solo try.
 Loading Twitter content React React Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 4:46pm Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 4:46pm 28' Jillaroos win their captain's challenge
 J By Jon Healy
 The Kiwi Ferns regather Chantay Kiria-Ratu's bomb and offload back in-field.
 Australia is pinged for a knock-on in the scrap for the ball, but the Jillaroos challenge and it's spot-on.
 Instead of a fresh set from 20 metres out, the play goes back to the previous play the ball and this time Tamika Upton fields the bomb.
 React React Key Event
 Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 4:38pm Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 4:38pm Ex-Jillaroo Shannon Mato is over for New Zealand
 J By Jon Healy
 Back-to-back penalties put the Kiwi Ferns right on the attack and, from about 2 metres out, Ashleigh Quinlan spies a gap just off the ruck and hits a rampaging Shannon Mato to crash in over the top of Kezie Apps.
 Mato won the last World Cup alongside Apps and a slew of the other Jillaroos four years ago.
 React React Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 4:38pm Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 4:38pm 22' Kiwi Ferns signalling their intent
 J By Jon Healy
 New Zealand hasn't had much of a chance to turn it on, but there's clearly a plan to spread the ball wide to get out of trouble.
 This time it pits Mele Hufanga against Tarryn Aiken in the sort of match-up that would be illegal on Main Event.
 Fortunately the rest of the defence arrives to help her out.
 React React Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 4:35pm Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 4:35pm World Cup hydration breaks are back, baby
 J By Jon Healy
 When I turned up at the ground today, I was pretty worried about the weather.
 It is properly hot and very classically muggy in Brisbane. I'd hate to be playing footy in mid-November in the sub-stropics.
 So the tournament has instituted hydration breaks halfway through each half, which is a good idea, but seems a little redundant when the Jillaroos are scoring every three minutes.
 React React Key Event
 Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 4:31pm Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 4:31pm JESS SERGIS FROM LONG RANGE!
 J By Jon Healy
 It's a 70-metre effort from Jessica Sergis as she pops up on the left side of the field for a yardage carry, but explodes through the tackle of Raecene McGregor and can't be halted.
 (Getty) The dummy-half pass from Jesse Southwell was definitely forward, but the on-field officials missed it.
 You know who doesn't miss? Jesse Southwell. She slots another, albeit from right in front, to make it 4/4 and 24-0.
 React React Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 4:30pm Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 4:30pm Are you listening, Peter?
 J By Jon Healy
 It’s ironic that the NRL is claiming to be trying to grow the game in the USA, and yet the only way to watch the World Cup games here is to pay for some obscure streaming service. You would think they would be making it very easy to watch.
 - Lief 
 I'll pass this on to Mr V'landys and get you sorted, Lief.
 React React Key Event
 Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 4:26pm Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 4:26pm You'll believe Chap-man can fly!!
 J By Jon Healy
 (Getty) The Jillaroos look like they've never met in the build-up, but when Jesse Southwell's offload hits the deck out on the left, Isabelle Kelly makes a lovely pick-up off her bootlaces and finds Jaime Chapman outside her.
 There's still a lot of work for the winger to do as the defence closes in, but she produces a glorious leap and one-and-a-half-handed putdown out on the wing.
 What an effort from Chapman to complete the double.
 Loading Twitter content And again Jesse Southwell is perfect from out on the left. It's 18-0 to Australia after 16 minutes.
 React React Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 4:24pm Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 4:24pm 12' Signs of life from the Kiwi Ferns
 J By Jon Healy
 The last tackle looks like a mess from New Zealand but eventually the ball finds Raecene McGregor and she chips over the top for Golden Boot winner Stacey Waaka to leap over Isabelle Kelly.
 She offloads back to McGregor supporting back up through the middle, but the halfback knocks on with the tryline almost within reach.
 React React Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 4:20pm Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 4:20pm 9' Nothing offered in attack by New Zealand
 J By Jon Healy
 The Kiwi Ferns have a full set deep in Australian territory, but never threaten and eventually the ball dies with five-eighth Chantay Kiria-Ratu.
 React React Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 4:20pm Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 4:20pm 7' The Jillaroos make a meal of the kick-off
 J By Jon Healy
 It's a third straight kick-off to exactly the same spot, but the Jillaroos get themselves in a tangle trying to field it.
 The ball cleared Tarryn Aiken and prop Simaima Taufa was happy to take the catch and the hit-up, but fullback Tamika Upton decided she needed help and instead barrelled into her, knocking the ball dead.
 React React Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 4:16pm Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 4:16pm Shaylee's Bent them back!
 J By Jon Healy
 The Jillaroos march upfield off a penalty and once again go to work.
 The ball comes right and Tarryn Aiken turns Shaylee Bent back under. The Aussie back rower bobbles the pass and it appears to freeze Georgia Hale as Bent breaks through and dives in from close range.
 React React Key Event
 Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 4:13pm Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 4:13pm TRY! The Jillaroos are over in the second minute!!
 J By Jon Healy
 Australia packs a scrum wide on the right, giving them the entire width of the field to get their footy on.
 The shift isn't that quick, and it looks like Mackenzie Wiki may have it covered as Tamika Upton gives Jaime Chapman early ball, but Chapman stutter steps, breaks wide and muscles her way through three Ferns to get the ball down brilliantly.
 Loading Twitter content Jesse Southwell converts from the left sideline, and the Jillaroos lead 6-0.
 React React Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 4:13pm Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 4:13pm 2' Aussies straight onto the attack
 J By Jon Healy
 New Zealand tries to spin it left to get out of trouble, but Kaiyah Atai knocks it on cold.
 The back rower was out on the wing and couldn't handle a simple pass.
 React React Key Event
 Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 4:10pm Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 4:10pm 1' New Zealand kicks us off
 J By Jon Healy
 And Simaima Taufa takes the first charge into a trio of Ferns.
 It's a strong first set by the Aussies and the kick chase follows it up by dominating Leianne Tufuga.
 React React Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 4:09pm Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 4:09pm Face to face in the haka
 J By Jon Healy
 Shannon Mato, a former World Cup winner with the Jillaroos, leads the Kiwi Ferns in an advance during the haka.
 And the Jillaroos respond.
 Loading Twitter content They come face to face, before Mato embraces Sariah Paki and the teams get in some last-minute warm-ups before kick-off.
 React React Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 4:02pm Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 4:02pm Here come the teams
 J By Jon Healy
 The Jillaroos and Kiwi Ferns are out on Lang Park and lined up for the anthems.
 And now it's time for New Zealand's haka.
 React React Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 3:42pm Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 3:42pm What's the deal with the Golden Boot?
 J By Jon Healy
 So, in a year with only a handful of international rugby league games, the award for the best player in men's international rugby league was given to a player who played one and a half games, BEFORE the most important international game of the year in which he would have been in direct competition with his closest rival for the award.
 Cool.
 At least Stacey Waaka winning the women's award was more up-and-shut, but still bizarre behaviour by International Rugby League.
 The Rugby League World Cup final should have solved the Golden Boot battle 
 React React Key Event
 Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 3:34pm Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 3:34pm How did the Jillaroos and Kiwi Ferns get here?
 J By Jon Healy
 (Getty) There was nothing resembling a speed bump for the Aussie women through the group stages as they won their three games against Samoa, England and Wales by a combined 242-6.
 Then came the semifinal against Fiji, which was supposed to be a similar story but the Bulikula staged an early ambush for an early 8-0 lead. It may not sound like much, but it wasn't just the score, it was the way Fiji went about it, dominating with physicality and skill.
 The Jillaroos eventually resettled for a 30-14 win, and more than a few of them said it was just the sort of hit-out they needed before the final.
 (Getty) Fiji was also right in the game against the Kiwi Ferns to kick off their tournament, before a last-minute Leianne Tufuga try gave New Zealand an 18-12 win.
 Then they went 92-0 over France, 40-12 over Papua New Guinea, and 32-0 over Samoa.
 Pretty similar journeys, albeit in reverse order, for both teams. So hopefully it leads to a very even contest this afternoon.
 React React Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 3:25pm Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 3:25pm Who has won the women's World Cup finals?
 J By Jon Healy
 The Australians and the New Zealand have split all six women's world titles since they started playing World Cups back in 2000.
 The Kiwi Ferns won the first three, before the Jillaroos won in 2013, 2017 and 2022.
 2000: New Zealand 26-4 Great Britain
 2003: New Zealand 58-0 New Zealand Māori
 2008: New Zealand 34-0 Australia
 2013: Australia 22-12 New Zealand
 2017: Australia 23-16 New Zealand
 2022: Australia 54-4 New Zealand
 2026: Australia vs New Zealand 
 So this afternoon will be the tie-breaker.
 React React Key Event
 Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 3:17pm Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 3:17pm We've already had one RLWC final
 J By Jon Healy
 The Jillaroos and Kangaroos haven't been the only ones representing Australia at this Rugby League World Cup.
 The Wheelaroos have also wrapped up their campaign with third place in the wheelchair event, while England beat France the final.
 Spectacular try helps England to Wheelchair Rugby League World Cup glory 
 React React Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 3:09pm Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 3:09pm LATE MAIL: Jillaroos' big change confirmed
 J By Jon Healy
 (NRL.com) The only change for either of these teams is a massive call by Jillaroos coach Jess Skinner, subbing out five-eighth Jocelyn Kelleher for Jesse Southwell.
 Southwell only played in the 124-6 win over Wales, while Kelleher has been one of Australia's best throughout the tournament, pairing perfectly with Sydney Roosters' premiership-winning teammate Tarryn Aiken.
 Not only has Kelleher lost her starting gig, she's been completely cut from the 17.
 Brutal.
 Jillaroos spring a surprise as teams are named for World Cup finals 
 React React Key Event
 Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 3:04pm Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 3:04pm When do the finals kick off?
 J By Jon Healy
 The women's final between Australia and New Zealand is first up from 3:10pm AEST .
 Then there will be a little bit of a gap to the men's decider, from 6:35pm AEST .
 React React Key Event
 Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 2:33pm Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 2:33pm It's World Cup final day!
 J By Jon Healy
 Hello and welcome to ABC Sport's live coverage of today's men's and women's Rugby League World Cup finals.
 The Aussie Jillaroos and Kangaroos are up against their New Zealand rivals in both deciders at Lang Park.
 We'll bring you every moment as a marathon rugby league season comes to an end in searing heat and humidity in Brisbane.
 React React Timeline 
 Live: Australia Kangaroos vs New Zealand Kiwis 
 Pinned
 Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 7:05pm Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 7:05pm Sun 15 Nov 2026 at 7:05pm 
 Here come the teams
